notes: The REST limit parameter becomes first, and page_info becomes the after cursor taken from pageInfo.endCursor.
A single request returns at most 250 nodes. Above that, page or use a bulk operation.
REST filter parameters are not arguments one for one. Most become terms in the query search string, which accepts fields such as product_type, vendor, status, created_at, title and barcode.
sortKey defaults to ID and should match the field you filter on, or the query gets slower as the catalogue grows.
Fields are not returned unless you ask for them. A REST caller that read an undocumented field gets nothing back until that field is named.
The numeric REST id becomes a GID. Take it from the admin_graphql_api_id property on the REST payload rather than building the string yourself.
The return type is nullable, so a product that does not exist comes back as null inside a 200 response, not as a 404.
The argument is product of type ProductCreateInput. The input argument of type ProductInput is deprecated, and Shopify's own migration examples still show the deprecated form.
Variants cannot be created here. Create the product, then call productVariantsBulkCreate.
Products are created unpublished. Publishing is a separate publishablePublish call.
Above 50,000 variants in a store, no more than 1,000 new variants can be created per day.
The argument is product of type ProductUpdateInput. The input argument of type ProductInput is deprecated.
Variants cannot be updated here. Use productVariantsBulkUpdate for prices and variant detail.
A REST product update that also removed images has no equivalent here. Media deletion is its own call.
Deletion is permanent and takes variants, media, publications and inventory items with it.
For a product with many variants across several locations, pass synchronous false and follow the returned ProductDeleteOperation, or the call can time out.
